newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK elected chamber fights to pass residency laws.
newsitem.headline: HK elected chamber fights to pass residency laws.

text.p: Hong Kong lawmakers on Wednesday agreed to urge the government to submit a bill on residency rights so that it can be made into law before the British-ruled territory reverts to China at midnight June 30.
The motion over "right of abode", or permanent residency in Hong Kong after July 1, was passed by a vote of 23 against 22.
The motion defies China's wish to have the right of abode bill passed before July 1 by the Beijing-backed provisional legislature, which will replace the elected chamber upon the handover.
Beijing set the rules on who would qualify for "right of abode" in Hong Kong in a document issued in April.
But the current British colonial government has repeatedly opposed China's plan, warning that if the bill were to be handled by the interim chamber before July 1, it would invite legal challenges.
Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp opposes the interim chamber and has vowed to sue it if it tries to pass laws before July 1.
Secretary for Security Peter Lai told legislators the government was not yet ready to table such a bill and questioned the wisdom of rushing through a bill which could be revoked.

"Can we be sure that any right of abode bill passed by this council will not be 'dishonoured' in the future, hence creating more uncertainty for those whose immigration status wil be directly affected?" he said.
The right of abode issue is crucial for 750,000 Hong Kong people who have foreign citizenship but who want to know whether they can keep their permanent resident status in Hong Kong after July 1.
